title: india stocks log fifth weekly loss oil fears grip markets 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - India's equity benchmarks fell for a fifth consecutive week on Friday, as the escalating Middle East conflict pushed crude oil ​prices higher, raising concerns about inflation and global interest rates.
The Nifty ‌50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 dropped 0.34% to 23,398.1 and the BSE Sensex (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 lost 0.16% to 74,781.76. Both indexes fell over 2% this week and about 4.8% over the last five weeks.
The sell-off was broad-based, with fourteen ​of the 16 major sectors logging weekly losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 and ​mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 also lost 0.9% and 1.4%. The Indian rupee weakened 1% too this week, ⁠marking its sharpest weekly drop since mid-May.
Brent crude futures have surged over ​8% to $104 per barrel so far this week, as attacks on tankers in the ​Strait of Hormuz intensified and Iran-aligned Houthis threatened Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea as well.
"Such a sharp surge in Brent crude was not anticipated by the markets. Unless the Middle ​East crisis is resolved and Brent crude eases substantially, markets are in for a ​longer period of subdued performance," said Ambareesh Baliga, independent market analyst based in Mumbai.
Rising oil ‌prices ⁠inflamed inflation fears, sending global bond yields to multi-year highs. Higher bond yields typically reduce the appeal of risk assets such as equities for investors.
Heavyweight Financials (.NIFTYFIN)
, opens new tab
 lost 1.9% this week, with top private-sector lenders HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS)
, opens new tab
 and ICICI Bank (ICBK.NS)
, opens new tab
 dropping 0.5% and ​3.1% respectively. HDFC Bank fell ​for a sixth ⁠week in a row as uncertainty over its CEO succession continued.
Reliance Industries(RELI.NS)
, opens new tab
, the third highest weighted stock on the benchmark Nifty ​50, also lost 4.9% this week.
India's IT index(.NIFTYIT)
, opens new tab
 slumped 5.8% in ​its biggest ⁠weekly percentage drop since April. It was the biggest loser among major sub-sectors, weighed down by prospects of a Fed rate hike next week.
Investors await U.S. consumer inflation ⁠data later ​on Friday, seen as a key influence on ​next week's Fed interest rate decision.
Indian markets are closed on Monday for a local holiday.
